After its flotation, he established Fullbrook Thorpe Investments with Andrew Borkowski and his son Tom to invest family capital across privately held businesses.

biography.html: Andrew Derrick Leaver, known as Andy, is a British pharmaceutical entrepreneur based in Monaco. He founded Clinigen, bringing together drug-supply and pharmaceutical businesses he owned with his wife, Linda. After its flotation, he established Fullbrook Thorpe Investments with Andrew Borkowski and his son Tom to invest family capital across privately held businesses.

long_biography.plain_text:
Through Fullbrook Thorpe, Andrew Leaver helped fund Bionical's expansion in Britain and the United States. The investment financed its purchases of Nottingham-based North 51 and American engagement specialist McCallan Health, alongside capital for further growth. Bionical supplied services to pharmaceutical companies, broadening the healthcare interests in his portfolio.

His investment partnerships also extended to food manufacturing. Fullbrook Thorpe joined LDC in buying Addo Food Group, a producer of chilled savoury pastries for British supermarkets. The existing management team, led by Chris Peters, continued running the business; the investment supported plans for product development and expansion into new markets.

confidence.reason: Two transaction advisers describe completed investments and distinguish funded purchases from future growth plans.
